'''Arto Kustaa Salomaa''' (6 June 1934 – 26 January 2025) was a Finnish mathematician and computer scientist.  His research career, which spanned over 40 years, was focused on [[formal languages]] and [[automata theory]].

==Early life and education==
Salomaa was born in [[Turku]], Finland on 6 June 1934. He earned a [[Bachelor's degree]] from the [[University of Turku]] in 1954 and a [[PhD]] from the same university in 1960. Salomaa's father was a professor of philosophy at the [[University of Turku]].<ref name=Karhumaki>{{cite journal|last=Karhumäki|first=J.|doi=10.1006/inco.1998.2760|title=A short biography of Arto Salomaa|journal=[[Information and Computation]]|volume=151|issue=1–2|year=1991|pages=2–4|doi-access=free}}</ref> Salomaa was introduced to the theory of automata and formal languages during seminars at [[University of California, Berkeley|Berkeley]] given by [[John Myhill]] in 1957.<ref name="Arto-eatcs">{{cite journal|first=A.|last=Salomaa|title=Myhill, Turku and Sauna Poetry: Recollections arising from the EATCS Award|journal=[[Bulletin of the European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]]|volume=84|year=2004|pages=12–15}}</ref>

==Career==
In 1965 Salomaa became a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Turku]], a position he retired from in 1999. He also spent two years in the late 1960s at the [[University of Western Ontario]] in [[London, Ontario|London]], Ontario, Canada, and two years in the 1970s at [[Aarhus University]] in [[Aarhus]], Denmark.<ref name=Karhumaki/><ref name=salomaa>{{citation|first=A.|last= Salomaa|contribution=Events and Languages|title=People and Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science|editor-first=C. S.|editor-last=Calude|pages=253–273|publisher=[[Springer-Verlag|Springer]]|year=1999}}.</ref>

Salomaa was president of the [[EATCS|European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]] from 1979 until 1985.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eatcs.org/index.php/about-the-association/article/497 |title=Silver Jubilee of EATCS |first1=Ute |last1=Brauer |first2=Wilfried |last2=Brauer |publisher=EATCS |year=1997 |accessdate=November 24, 2013 |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111212020951/http://eatcs.org/index.php/about-the-association/article/497 |archivedate=December 12, 2011 }}</ref>

==Publications==
Salomaa authored or co-authored 46 textbooks, including ''[[Automata theory|Theory of Automata]]'' (1969), ''[[Formal languages|Formal Languages]]'' (1973), ''The Mathematical Theory of [[L Systems|L-Systems]]'' (1980, with [[Grzegorz Rozenberg]]), ''Jewels of Formal Language Theory'' (1981) ''[[Public key cryptography|Public-Key Cryptography]]'' (1990) and ''[[DNA computing|DNA Computing]]'' (1998, with [[Grzegorz Rozenberg]] and [[Gheorghe Paun]]). With [[Grzegorz Rozenberg|Rozenberg]], Salomaa edited the ''Handbook of Formal Languages'' (1997), a 3-volume, 2000-page reference on [[Formal language|formal language theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Handbook of Formal Languages'' by Grzegorz Rozenberg and Arto Salomaa|first=Gabriel|last= Infante-Lopez|journal=Journal of Logic, Language and Information|volume=14|issue=4|year=2005|pages=457–466|jstor=40180402}}</ref> These books have often become standard references in their respective areas. For example, ''Formal Languages'' was reported in 1991 to be among the 100 most cited texts in mathematics.<ref name=Karhumaki/>

Salomaa published over 400 articles in scientific journals during his professional career.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Karhumäki |first=Juhani |author-link=Juhani Karhumäki |date=2014-08-26 |title=A survey of Arto's achievements |url=https://dlt2014.sciencesconf.org/conference/dlt2014/pages/Invited_special_Karhumaki.pdf |journal=[[International Conference on Developments in Language Theory]] |issue=18}}</ref> He also authored non-scientific articles such as "What computer scientists should know about sauna".<ref>{{cite journal|first=A.|last=Salomaa|title=What computer scientists should know about sauna|journal=Bulletin of the European Association of Theoretical Computer Science |volume=15|year=1981|pages=8–21}}</ref> From his retirement until 2014, Salomaa published over 100 scientific articles.<ref name=":0" />

==Personal life and death==
Salomaa married in 1959.<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url=http://www.math.utu.fi/projects/staff/asalomaa/cvarto.html |title=Curriculum Vitae |first=Arto |last=Salomaa |accessdate=2018-07-04}}.</ref> He had two children, Kirsti and [[Kai Salomaa|Kai]],<ref name="cv" /> the latter of whom is a professor of Computer Science at [[Queen's University at Kingston]] and also works in the field of formal languages and automata theory.<ref>{{cite web|accessdate=April 21, 2014 |url=http://www.cs.queensu.ca/~ksalomaa/ |title=Kai T. Salomaa |publisher=[[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140421082706/http://research.cs.queensu.ca/~ksalomaa/ |archivedate=April 21, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Salomaa died on 26 January 2025, at the age of 90.<ref>Kuolleet, Ilkka-Pohjalainen, p. 14, 28 January 2025</ref> The [[Research Council of Finland]] reported his death two days later in a press release, on 28 January.<ref name="obit">{{cite web|url=https://www.aka.fi/en/about-us/whats-new/press-releases/2025/arto-salomaa-academician-of-science-dies-at-90/|title=Arto Salomaa, Academian of Science, dies at 90|accessdate=2025-01-28}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Salomaa was awarded the title of [[Academician]] by the [[Academy of Finland]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aka.fi/en/about-us/scientists-behind-the-research/academicians-of-science/finnish-academicians-of-science/ |title=Finnish Academicians of Science — Academy of Finland |access-date=2018-07-07 |archive-date=2019-03-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190324041421/https://www.aka.fi/en/about-us/scientists-behind-the-research/academicians-of-science/finnish-academicians-of-science/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="academy">Academy of Finland, {{cite web|url=http://www.aka.fi/en-GB/A/Academy-of-Finland/Who-we-are/Academicians/ |title=Academicians &#124; Academy of Finland |accessdate=2014-06-02 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140329152210/http://www.aka.fi/en-GB/A/Academy-of-Finland/Who-we-are/Academicians/ |archivedate=2014-03-29 }}.</ref> one of twelve living Finnish individuals awarded the title. He also received the [[EATCS Award]] in 2004.<ref name=eatcs>{{citation|first=Jan|last=van Leeuwen|authorlink=Jan van Leeuwen|title=The distinguished achievement award: EATCS Award 2004|journal=Bulletin of the European Association for Theoretical Computer Science|volume=84|year=2004|pages=10–11}}</ref> Salomaa received seven honorary degrees.<ref name=eatcs/> On 13 June 2013, Salomaa was awarded a Doctor Honoris Causa from the [[University of Western Ontario]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.csd.uwo.ca/news/arto_salomaa.html |title=Arto Salomaa - Computer Science - Western University |publisher=Computer Science Department, [[University of Western Ontario]] |accessdate=2018-07-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180708015627/http://www.csd.uwo.ca/news/arto_salomaa.html |archive-date=2018-07-08 |url-status=dead }}.</ref>
